items.title: My First Impressions of Fable 5.2
items.summary:
My First Impressions of Fable 5.2

I’ve been using it for a few hours now, and I have a few thoughts on the new Fable 5.2:

1. The weirdest RL I've ever seen. On some tasks it's a genius; on others, it's as dumb as a shrimp. In pure coding tasks, it's at least on par with Opus 5.5. But ask it to reason through something non-standard that isn't coding-related, and its output drops to the level of GPT-3.5. I asked both Fable 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra to flesh out a project idea and Fable’s response was complete garbage

2.  Fable models have always been notorious for mediocre taste - worse than Opus. This time, Fable surprised me with a complete absence of it. In a long list, it inexplicably added two separate pagination controls: one expands the currently loaded list of data, and the second one underneath fetches new content. On top of that, you can see plenty of demos on X with pretty mediocre results that are even worse than Opus

3. It seems to be the most token-hungry model in the world. The advertised price cut makes zero sense when Fable 5.2 burns through four times more tokens than 5.1

4. The most pedantic model yet. It constantly tries to prove you wrong. Tell it that snow is white, and it will find a million reasons why that's not entirely accurate. GPT-6 Astra had this annoying trait as well

5. It’s noticeably faster. On medium effort, it responds almost instantaneously

6. Fable 5.5 has picked up a trait that used to belong to Sonnet 5.5 - diligence. Once it takes on a task, it will check and iterate multiple times until it achieves a solid result

7. For coding tasks, there is zero difference compared to Opus 5.5. Across all other aspects, Opus 5.5 is, in my subjective view, superior to Fable 5.5

I’ve never really liked Fable models. There’s not much point to them. They’re stubborn, weighed down by guardrail filters, have poor taste, and are expensive, token-hungry, and in some areas worse than the Opus lineup. This one is no exception. In my view, the new Fable 5.2 makes no sense, and I think I understand why they called this release 5.2 rather than 5.5. A revolutionary leap like the jump from Opus 5 to 5.5 just didn't happen

items.title: Among Anthropic models, tool use rises with VIALS-AA Score. From Haiku 5.5 to Fable 5.2, average tool calls per task cli
items.summary:
Among Anthropic models, tool use rises with VIALS-AA Score. From Haiku 5.5 to Fable 5.2, average tool calls per task climb from ~21 to ~37, with most of that gain to image viewing. Image views rise ~30% from Opus to Fable, while its code-execution calls rises only ~5%.

OpenAI models take the opposite approach: GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6.1 Terra and GPT-6 Luna all make fewer tool calls than Haiku. Astra, the highest scoring of them, makes the fewest.

items.title: People should always be in control of the future.
items.summary:
People should always be in control of the future.

OpenAI is against the notion that it would be acceptable for people to be relegated to a role of doing things that “AI systems think makes sense to reward in humans”.

People should not cede control of the future to superintelligence, and that requirement should ultimately constrain AI progress.

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.
